an4.97:2.2: This passage clarifies the common phrase, “one who practices in line with the teaching” (_dhammānudhammappaṭipanna_). The _dhamma_ here is specifically the “teaching” (rather than “principle” or “moral law”). In fact, though the compound masks the number, it should probably be plural (“teachings”), although the Pali is not consistent on this detail. When at [snp1.3:35.2]() we encounter a similar phrase with compound resolved, the initial element is locative plural (_dhammesu_) suggesting the literal rendering, “one who, in respect of the teachings, practices according to the teachings”. The gloss on that passage in the Niddesa explains “teachings” as the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, etc. (i.e. the 37 wings of awakening), and what is in line with the teachings as right practice, including ethics, sense restraint, moderation in eating, wakefulness, and situational awareness, namely the fundamentals of the “gradual training” that one undertakes after hearing the teaching ([cnd23:318.1]()).
